editorial:
Imagine trying to navigate high school while keeping your true self a secret. You follow Jun, a quiet guy who is gay but not ready to tell the world. Things get messy when Sae, a girl who loves reading romance stories about men, asks him out. Since he doesn't want to cause a scene, he says yes, but he is already dating another guy named Makoto. It creates this awkward, tense vibe where you really feel Jun's stress as he tries to balance two completely different relationships without getting caught.

The acting feels very real and doesn't feel like a cheesy teen movie. You will love how the film handles the slow build-up of tension, though some might find the middle part a bit slow. If you enjoy stories about identity and first loves, you should definitely check this out. To get the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for those crisp visuals, or just rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night at home.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Sae finds out the truth about Jun and Makoto. Instead of a huge fight, it leads to an honest conversation where Jun finally stops hiding. He realizes he cannot keep lying to people he cares about. The movie ends with him accepting his identity and finding a way to move forward with a clear conscience, leaving the viewers feeling hopeful about his future growth.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about young love and finding yourself.
